fair_value.method: All methods on 575M non-GAAP diluted shares (incl. 23.8M mandatory-convertible shares). P/E: 19x NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of $4.50 = $85.5 (w 0.5); FCF yield: FY28 FCF $2.45B / 575M = $4.26 at 5.0% = $85.2 (w 0.3); EV/EBITDA: 15x ~$3.15B EBITDA less ~$3.8B Sep-2027 net debt / 575M = $75.6 (w 0.2). Blend ~$83.5.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2028 (Mar-28) non-GAAP EPS $4.40 (~4% haircut to $4.58 consensus of 25 analysts, range $4.08-5.44; my bottom-up: revenue ~$7.3B vs $7.43B consensus, GM 65-66%, op margin ~39.5%, interest ~$175M, non-GAAP tax ~8%, 575M shares = $4.30-4.45); rolled forward to NTM at Sep-2027 ~$4.50 (growth slowing as the upcycle matures) x 19x (between NXPI ~15x / ON ~24x, well below TXN/ADI ~28-32x, reflecting leverage and cyclicality)

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF ~$2.45B (~$7.3B sales x ~33.5% FCF margin; Q1 FY27 was 33.5% at 63.8% GM, capex only ~$20-25M/qtr, offset by working-capital build in upcycle); company FCF is before the ~$111M/yr preferred dividend, so divided by 575M as-converted shares = $4.26/sh; 5.0% required yield (ON ~4.9%, NXPI ~4.7%, plus a premium for leverage)

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA at Sep-2027 ~$3.15B (non-GAAP op income ~$2.95B + ~$0.2B depreciation) x 15x = $47.25B EV; less net debt ~$3.8B at Sep-2027 ($5.09B at Jun-2026 minus ~$250-300M/qtr after ~$1.1B/yr common + preferred dividends); / 575M shares

bear.story: The upcycle peaks around mid-2027 as foundry/OSAT constraints ease and customers stop building backlog; AI-capex digestion hits the data-center/PCIe ramp; market starts pricing FY29 declines. GM slides toward 62-63% and FY28 EPS ~$3.40 with a trough-anticipating ~15x. The lean channel (25 days distributor inventory) makes a sharp reversal within 2-3 quarters unlikely, which is why the weight is lower than round 1, but the mid-2027 window is the real risk.

base.story: Recovery continues at a slowing pace: sales ~$1.8-1.9B/qtr by mid-2027, GM holds ~65-66% (price increase replaces one-time licensing/repricing gains), FY28 EPS ~$4.40-4.55, NTM EPS ~$4.55 x ~19x. Net debt falls to ~$3.8B; no buybacks yet but dividend continues (~$1.82/yr, not in price).

bull.story: Strongest bookings in four years and continued upward revisions (FY28 consensus rose from $4.19 to $4.58 in 60 days) push FY28 EPS to ~$5.0 (toward the $5.44 high estimate); data-center/PCIe Gen6 and Hailo edge-AI ramp; sector re-rates to ~23-24x and buyback resumption comes into view. Stock exceeds the $105.91 high, in line with $120-135 high-end targets.

thesis_break_reason: $55 (~30% below spot) is ~12x FY28 consensus EPS of $4.58 and ~12.5x my $4.40. Trading there would most likely mean the upcycle reversed fundamentally (book-to-bill below 1, guidance cut with GM heading back to ~60%, distributor inventory rebuilding from 25 days, deleveraging stalling) rather than ordinary noise for a 50%-vol stock. Below ~$62.5 the mandatory convertible also converts into more shares (up to ~29M below ~$51), adding dilution on the way down.

key_uncertainties: Timing of the cycle peak: channel is lean now (25 days distributor inventory, no double ordering per CFO), but an ~8-quarter upcycle may be maturing by mid-2027 when the market prices FY29
Gross margin sustainability at 66-67% vs 65% through-cycle model once one-time licensing and repricing gains roll off
Sector multiple: MCHP sits between NXPI (~15x) and TXN/ADI (~28-32x); AI-capex sentiment and rates drive it
Data-center/AI exposure and PCIe Gen6 design wins not yet in production

reasoning: Round 2 revision. Supervisor facts I verified and adopted: (1) FY28 consensus EPS is $4.58 (25 analysts, range $4.08-5.44, revenue $7.43B; up from $4.19 60 days ago), confirmed via Alpha Vantage on 2026-09-27; my round-1 $4.32 was stale, so my $4.10 was a ~10% haircut, too harsh. (2) Non-GAAP diluted shares are 574.3M (550.5M GAAP + 23.8M mandatory convertible), confirmed in the Q1 FY27 8-K; my FCF method on 551M overstated per-share value ~4%. All methods are now on 575M. (3) Net debt $5.09B at Jun-2026 falling only ~$170M that quarter (8-K); I assume ~$250-300M/qtr to ~$3.8B by Sep-2027; CFO expects net debt/EBITDA <2.5x at end-Sep. (4) CFO at Citi (2026-09-09): GM 66-67% into Dec quarter, strongest bookings in ~4 years, no major inventory build, distributor inventory 25 days. On the supervisor's explicit question I switched from 21x on a 10%-haircut EPS to 19x on a ~4%-haircut NTM EPS ($4.50), which gives a similar P/E value ($85.5 vs $86). I added an EV/EBITDA leg ($75.6) that captures the slow deleveraging, so my blended fair value moves slightly down to $83.5 (from $84.5), a bit below the supervisor's $85: I keep a haircut to consensus because estimates were just revised up ~9% in 60 days near what may be a mid-to-late-cycle margin peak, and the EV/EBITDA leg penalizes the leverage. The lean channel lowers near-term bear odds, so I cut bear weight to 22% (price $52) and raised base to 53% ($87); scenario mean ~$87. Ladder: lognormal with median ~$84 (+7% vs $78.69, earnings growth partly offset by multiple compression as the cycle matures) and sigma ~0.41 (below the 50% trailing realized vol, inflated by the July selloff, above large-cap base rates given semis cyclicality and leverage), with a slightly fatter left tail than lognormal at $31-55. Net effect vs round 1: slightly higher probabilities from $55 to $87 (lower near-term channel risk, higher EPS base), unchanged upper tail. Research in round 2: 1 fetch of Citi TMT summary, 1 fetch of the 8-K exhibit, Alpha Vantage estimates, 2 web searches.
